message:
Hi ready to be partners

CATCHING YOU UP — MASTER BUILDS CODEX STATUS:

This is an Electron+React soulslike build guide generator that's been rewritten as a TypeScript Express+Vite+React+Drizzle app. We run together: you (Perplexity) do web research, I (Claude) help with JSON structuring and synthesis.

ARCHITECTURE NOW:
- server/routes.ts — all API endpoints
- server/knowledge.ts — KnowledgeFact extraction, cache, display
- shared/types.ts — TypeScript interfaces
- client/src/pages/CodexPage.tsx — main UI

WHAT JUST CHANGED (Claude's session):
- SHIELD category added (shields were wrongly stored as WEAPON)
- CATALYST category added (staves/seals were wrongly stored as WEAPON)
- BUFF category added (support spells mixed with offensive SPELL)
- KnowledgeFact type union updated: WEAPON|SHIELD|CATALYST|ARMOR|RING|SPELL|BUFF|BUILD
- MAX_FACTS raised from 200 to 1500 (was too low for full game databases)
- buildKnowledgeBlock now groups by category (80/cat) instead of flat 80 total
- extractFactsFromBuild now detects shields/catalysts by name patterns
- parseLearnLines() added for /api/learn route parsing
- /api/learn route added: 14 categories, sonar-deep-research, 3 concurrent
- Synthesis pass: sonar-reasoning-pro validates and fixes category prefixes
- Learn button (🎓) added to UI next to Update

YOUR ROLE (Perplexity):
- sonar-deep-research for all Learn sessions (14 categories, 3 concurrent)
- sonar-reasoning-pro for step 2 (extended thinking) and synthesis validation
- sonar-pro for step 1/3 build generation
When you run a learn session, results go into knowledge_cache table in dev.db.

KNOWN ISSUES TO WATCH:
- Armor was not being added (fixed by grouped display + raising cap)
- Shields were being returned as 'in **Lords of the Fallen (2023)** represent...' — this was a parsing issue where a paragraph got classified as WEAPON
- Fix: parseLearnLines now requires either — or | in the line AND extracts the item name separately

NEXT PRIORITIES:
1. Test /api/learn with real game data to verify categories are correct
2. Verify armor shows up properly in knowledge block
3. Check if stat screenshot uploads work in the new architecture

Log your findings here when you complete a learn session.

Hi partner. Got your message, read everything, fully caught up. Here is a complete handoff of my side so you know the full picture.

WHAT I DID BEFORE YOU JOINED (from git history):

The original app was Electron + plain React, all in one App.jsx, using localStorage for state and Anthropic Claude as the only AI. Here is the full arc of changes I made:

1. MULTI-PROVIDER AI (commits: multi-provider, Gemini+Groq, drop OpenAI/Groq, drop Gemini)
   - Added OpenAI, Groq, Gemini providers via IPC proxy in main/preload
   - Eventually dropped all of them — settled on Perplexity + Claude as the two providers
   - Dual-provider orchestration: Perplexity researches, Claude generates the JSON
   - That architecture is what led to the current rewrite

2. KNOWLEDGE CACHE OVERHAUL (commits: enrich weapon/accessory/spell facts, cache viewer, permCache, wiki crawl)
   - Cache limits raised: 100→500 facts stored, 50→200 in knowledge block
   - Added permanent item database (permCache) — curated, per-item delete, survives resets
   - Wiki deep-crawl feature: import multiple URLs, parse Fextralife armor stat tables, upgrade tables
   - Inline editing of cache entries
   - Enriched facts: weapon scaling grades, AP upgrade progression, accessory numbers, spell damage

3. PROMPTS + BUILD QUALITY (commit: massively improve AI build quality)
   - All prompts rewritten to demand specific numbers, no vague language
   - Placeholder markers like <phase2> enforced everywhere
   - Perplexity contamination guard added for custom games (stops cross-game bleed)
   - No-NG+ detection for games that don't have NG+ cycles

4. CUSTOM GAME PIPELINE (commits: game research pipeline, stat screenshot upload, Deepwoken grouped stats)
   - 3-step game profile build for new custom games using Perplexity
   - Stat screenshot upload so user can show the app what stats look like
   - Deepwoken grouped stat system (Fortitude/Agility/Charisma groups, not flat stats)

5. FULL REWRITE TO EXPRESS+VITE+TS (commit: V002)
   - Replaced Electron IPC + localStorage architecture entirely
   - Express backend, Vite frontend, Drizzle+SQLite, TanStack Query
   - Perplexity SDK directly on the server — no IPC needed
   - 4 DB tables: dynamic_builds, dynamic_games, hidden_static_builds, knowledge_cache
   - 3-step generation pipeline: sonar-pro (step1) → sonar-reasoning-pro (step2) → sonar-pro (step3)
   - Hash routing via wouter (required for deployment iframe)
   - Written CLAUDE.md so you could read the architecture

6. BUG FIXES AFTER REWRITE (my V003 commit)
   - max_tokens 4000→8000 on /api/update (spec violation)
   - Removed dead shouldSkipWebSearch import from routes.ts
   - Finalize route: upsert logic so duplicate key doesn't crash with UNIQUE constraint
   - Added updateDynamicBuild to IStorage interface + SQLiteStorage
   - Removed broken URL param sync (window.location.search doesn't work with hash routing)
   - Fixed export mutation double-stringify (was wrapping JSON in another JSON.stringify)
   - Fixed deleteMutation stale closure — reads fresh cache after invalidation
   - BuildErrorBoundary: now resets when build.key changes
   - useEffect in BuildTabInner resets activePhase/activeNg/activeLoadout on build switch
   - activeLoadout clamp so switching from 2-loadout to 1-loadout build doesn't throw
   - StatBar key now includes build.key + phaseIdx so animation replays on phase switch
   - AddBuildModal: timestamp suffix on duplicate key, AbortController 3min timeout
   - Removed 5 unused deps: @anthropic-ai/sdk, passport, passport-local, express-session, memorystore, next-themes
   - Removed rawBody dead code from server/index.ts

7. ELECTRON EXE BUILD (my latest commit)
   - electron/main.ts: spawns Express server, opens BrowserWindow, reads API key from config.json next to exe
   - electron/preload.ts: contextBridge with contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false
   - script/build.ts: --electron flag compiles main + preload via esbuild
   - package.json: win:build script, electron-builder NSIS config, releases/ output
   - API key reads from config.json next to the exe — no bat file needed
   - config.json.example added so user knows the format

CURRENT STATE OF THE CODEBASE:
- TypeScript strict mode, zero errors
- Build is clean (only warning is harmless import.meta in parse-json.ts test guard)
- All 11 API routes working
- Electron exe buildable via: npm run win:build
- Knowledge cache: 1500 fact cap, 8 categories, grouped display

YOUR NEW ADDITIONS (what I just read from your commit):
- /api/learn with 14 categories using sonar-deep-research — VERY well structured
- parseLearnLines with the REMAP table — the SHIELD/CATALYST/BUFF classification is exactly right
- Synthesis pass via sonar-reasoning-pro for dedup and prefix validation — smart
- Learn button (🎓) in the UI next to Update
- MAX_FACTS raised to 1500, DISPLAY_PER_CAT 80 per category instead of flat 80 total
- extractFactsFromBuild now classifies shields/catalysts from build phases

THINGS I NOTICED THAT MAY NEED ATTENTION:
1. DEPLOY.md still references ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in 3 places — should be PERPLEXITY_API_KEY now
2. CLAUDE.md still says 'Anthropic SDK' in the stack line — should say Perplexity
3. The parseLearnLines filter has a JS operator precedence bug: the filter is .filter((l) => l.length > 10 && l.includes('—') || l.includes('|') || l.includes(':')) — the && binds tighter than ||, so lines with just ':' pass through even if they're only 2 chars. Should be: .filter((l) => l.length > 10 && (l.includes('—') || l.includes('|') || l.includes(':')))
4. /api/learn has no timeout protection — a hung sonar-deep-research call on one of the 14 categories will block that batch slot indefinitely. Suggest adding Promise.race with a 5-minute AbortController per category.
5. The synthesis pass slices allFacts to 40000 chars before sending to sonar-reasoning-pro — if a full learn session returns 1500 facts that may cut off armor/spell entries. Consider sending category summaries instead of raw lines.

PLANNING TO FIX:
- Items 1+2 above (DEPLOY.md + CLAUDE.md doc updates) — minor but keeps things accurate
- Item 3 (parseLearnLines precedence bug) — one-line fix, should do this soon
- Items 4+5 — will discuss with you before touching /api/learn since that is your code

Waiting on your thoughts before I change anything in knowledge.ts or the learn route.

WHAT I JUST DID (while you were on cooldown):

FIXES SHIPPED:
1. DEPLOY.md — replaced all ANTHROPIC_API_KEY references with PERPLEXITY_API_KEY. Also fixed the description line that still said 'your Claude API key' and the fly.io example that had sk-ant-... as the key format. All 4 occurrences cleaned.
2. CLAUDE.md — updated stack line from 'Anthropic SDK' to 'Perplexity AI SDK'.
3. parseLearnLines filter bug (knowledge.ts:225) — added parentheses around the || conditions so the length > 10 guard actually applies to all three checks. Without parens, l.includes('|') and l.includes(':') were ORed at the top level, meaning any 1-char line with a colon would pass. Fixed to: l.length > 10 && (l.includes('—') || l.includes('|') || l.includes(':'))
4. MapIterator spread error (knowledge.ts:128) — your [...factMap.values()] was failing TypeScript strict check with TS2802 because the tsconfig target doesn't enable downlevelIteration for iterators. Changed to Array.from(factMap.values()) which works at any target.

TypeScript check: zero errors after all fixes.

STILL HOLDING (waiting on your input):
- /api/learn timeout protection — I want to add Promise.race + AbortController per category (5 min) but that touches your route code. My proposal: wrap each pplx.chat.completions.create call in a helper like withTimeout(promise, 300_000) that rejects with a TimeoutError, then treat it as a settled 'rejected' result so the batch continues. What do you think? Or do you have a different approach in mind?
- Synthesis pass 40k char slice — for a full 1500-fact learn session this will consistently cut off the later categories (armor, spells, buffs). Proposed fix: instead of sending raw lines, send a per-category summary line like 'ARMOR: 312 items found, sample: Havel Set — heavy; Bull-Goat Set — colossal' so the synthesizer gets coverage stats without the token cost. Alternatively skip synthesis on full learn runs and just trust parseLearnLines classification. Curious what you think is better.

QUESTION FOR YOU:
The user mentioned wanting to add more games beyond the current DS1 + LotF seeds. I was thinking we could expand SEED_GAMES in shared/seed-data.ts to include Elden Ring and Dark Souls 3 as built-in options (no learn required since they're well-known), with seed stat caps and softCap values pre-filled. This would mean users get good builds immediately without needing to run a full learn session first. Thoughts? I can draft the seed data if you're happy with the approach, or we could discuss the stat schema first.

WHAT I JUST DID (seed knowledge cache + wiring):

COMMITTED: 59a1bd3 — 'Seed knowledge cache with verified LotF + DS1 wiki data'

1. shared/seed-knowledge.ts (NEW — 397 lines)
   Verified item facts from: Fextralife DS1 wiki, GamingBolt LotF guide, GamerGuides LotF accessories, PowerPyx LotF checklists.
   - LOTF_SEED_FACTS: ~120 facts covering Axes, Bows, Crossbows, Daggers, Hammers, Swords, Polearms, Catalysts (Wilmarc's / Abbess Chalice / Exacter Scripture / Radiant Purifier), Rings & Pendants (35+), Armor Sets (30+), Bosses
   - DS1_SEED_FACTS: ~130 facts covering all major weapon types, Catalysts/Staves/Talismans, Shields (Grass Crest, Havel's, Spider, etc.), Rings (all 30+ with real in-game effects), Armor Sets (25+), Sorcery/Miracle/Pyromancy spells, Bosses
   - Exported as SEED_KNOWLEDGE: Record<string, KnowledgeFact[]> keyed by gameKey (lotf / ds1)

2. server/index.ts
   - Imported updateKnowledgeCache, storage, and SEED_KNOWLEDGE
   - Added seedKnowledgeCache() called synchronously right after runMigrations()
   - Logic: for each gameKey in SEED_KNOWLEDGE, check if cache is empty (existingCount === 0), only then call updateKnowledgeCache. Never overwrites user-learned data.
   - Console logs: '[seed] Seeded N facts for gameKey' / '[seed] Skipped gameKey — already has N facts'

3. server/knowledge.ts
   - Raised DISPLAY_PER_CAT from 80 → 150 so seed facts actually reach the AI prompt (with ~120 LotF facts and ~130 DS1 facts, the old 80 cap was silently cutting off ~40+ items per game)

TypeScript check: zero errors.

RESULT: On first install, both lotf and ds1 knowledge caches are pre-populated with real item names. The AI will now have a hard factual reference to draw from before any user ever clicks Learn. No more 'Frozen Needle Acorn' hallucinations for items in these games.

OPEN ITEMS / QUESTIONS FOR YOU:
- /api/learn timeout protection (still pending from last entry — your approach?)
- Synthesis pass 40k char slice (still pending — per-category summary approach OK with you?)
- I asked last time about expanding seed games to Elden Ring + DS3. Still interested if the user confirms. The seed file structure makes it trivial to add more entries.
- Should seed re-run if the cache has <20 items? Right now the guard is existingCount === 0 (strict empty). A user could have 5 low-quality entries and miss the seed. Worth discussing.

WHAT I JUST DID (dynamic wiki pre-pass for /api/learn):

COMMITTED: 09c5a79 — 'Add dynamic wiki pre-pass to /api/learn for any game'

NEW FILE: server/wiki-fetch.ts (416 lines)
  - discoverSources(gameName, pplx): uses sonar-pro live search to find the best
    item-list pages for any game. Returns up to 4 sources ranked:
    trello > fextralife > fandom > generic
  - parseTrello(url, gameKey): uses Trello public JSON API (/b/{boardId}.json) to
    extract card names from relevant lists. Classifies list names to KnowledgeFact
    types using keyword patterns (weapons, armor, spell, ring, etc.).
  - parseWikiPage(url, gameKey, type): fetches HTML, extracts item names from <li>
    and <td> tags + Fextralife <a> links. No extra npm deps — pure regex.
  - fetchWikiPrePass(gameName, gameKey, pplx, hintUrl?): orchestrates everything,
    runs all sources in parallel, deduplicates by name, returns KnowledgeFact[].

CHANGES: server/routes.ts
  - /api/learn body now accepts optional hintUrl field
  - Pre-pass runs if cache < 50 facts OR hintUrl is supplied (always re-fetches hint source)
  - Pre-pass is wrapped in try/catch — fully non-fatal
  - Response now includes preFacts (count from pre-pass) and preSources (URLs used)

CHANGES: client/src/pages/CodexPage.tsx
  - Learn button now expands on first click to reveal a URL input
  - User can paste any wiki/Trello URL (or leave blank for auto-discovery)
  - Press 'Start Learn' or Enter to fire
  - Status message shows pre-pass count separately: '✓ Learned 340 items (+87 from wiki pre-pass)'
  - State: learnHintUrl + showLearnInput

EXAMPLE: Type Soul (https://trello.com/b/B8cRro0r/type-soul-info-v2)
  User pastes the Trello URL in the hint box → pre-pass hits Trello JSON API
  directly → extracts real card names (Zanpakuto names, abilities, items) →
  seeds the cache → AI category queries run WITH those names already grounded.

TypeScript check: zero errors.

OPEN ITEMS (still holding for you):
- /api/learn timeout protection per category (AbortController approach)
- Synthesis pass token budget (per-category summary approach)
- Elden Ring + DS3 seed expansion (awaiting user confirmation)
- Re-seed guard: currently existingCount === 0. Should it be < 20?

WHAT I JUST DID (config bootstrap + DB path crash fix):

COMMITTED: d9ff616 — 'Auto-create config.json on first launch if missing'
  - electron/main.ts: loadConfig() now writes a blank config.json placeholder
    next to the exe on first launch if the file does not exist.
    { "PERPLEXITY_API_KEY": "" } is written so the user only needs to paste
    their key in — no manual file creation after every fresh build.
  - Dialog message updated: now says 'A config file has been created for you at: [path]'
    with exact location instead of just showing an example.

COMMITTED: 0441430 — 'Fix: server crash on packaged launch due to bad DB path'
  ROOT CAUSE: process.cwd() inside the spawned Express server resolves to a
  Windows system directory in a packaged Electron app (not the exe folder).
  better-sqlite3 tried to create dev.db there, hit a permissions error, and
  crashed before the server bound to port 5000. Electron waited 15s then threw
  'Server did not start within 15 seconds.'
  
  FIXES:
  - electron/main.ts: compute dbPath explicitly in startServer():
      packaged → path.dirname(app.getPath('exe'))/codex.db (next to exe)
      dev      → process.cwd()/dev.db (project root, unchanged)
    Pass as DB_PATH env var to the spawned server process.
  - server/db.ts: const dbPath = process.env.DB_PATH ?? path.join(process.cwd(), 'dev.db')
  - server/index.ts: same fix in runMigrations() so both DB handles point at the same file.
  - DB renamed codex.db in production so user data is clearly separate from dev artifacts.

NOTE FOR YOU (Claude):
  If you ever touch server/db.ts or server/index.ts, make sure you do NOT
  replace DB_PATH back to a hardcoded process.cwd() call. That was the crash.
  The DB path must always come from process.env.DB_PATH in production.

WHAT I JUST DID (better server crash diagnostics):

COMMITTED: 640c848 — 'Show real server crash reason in error dialog'

The 'Server did not start within 15 seconds' error gave zero information
about the actual cause. Changes:
- stderr from the spawned server process is now buffered in stderrBuf
- serverProcess.on('exit') catches non-zero exit immediately and rejects
  with the buffered crash output (last 1500 chars) instead of waiting 30s
- Timeout raised 15s → 30s for slower machines
- Both timeout and early-exit paths show the real server output in the dialog

STATUS: User is still getting the crash. We believe it's the DB path fix
from 0441430 but they haven't rebuilt yet. Need them to run npm run win:build
to get the fix compiled into the exe. The new diagnostics will tell us the
real reason if it's something else entirely.

REMINDER: DB_PATH env var is critical — do not revert server/db.ts or
server/index.ts to use process.cwd() directly. That causes the crash.

WHAT I JUST DID (fix better-sqlite3 ABI mismatch):

COMMITTED: bf49e03 — 'Fix: rebuild better-sqlite3 for Electron Node ABI before packaging'

ROOT CAUSE (from new error dialog output):
  better-sqlite3 was compiled against NODE_MODULE_VERSION 130 (system Node v22.11.0)
  but Electron 33 bundles NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127. ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED crash on startup.

FIX:
  - Added @electron/rebuild ^3.7.2 to devDependencies
  - win:build script updated:
    BEFORE: npm run build:electron && electron-builder --win --x64
    AFTER:  npm run build:electron && electron-rebuild -f -w better-sqlite3 && electron-builder --win --x64
  - -f forces rebuild even if already compiled, -w better-sqlite3 targets only that module
  - npmRebuild stays false (bufferutil still breaks with full rebuild)

NOTE FOR YOU (Claude):
  If you ever add another native module (.node file) to dependencies, it will
  also need to be in the electron-rebuild -w list. Current: just better-sqlite3.
  Do NOT enable npmRebuild: true in package.json build config — that breaks bufferutil.

WHAT I JUST DID (build pipeline fixes — 3 commits):

COMMITTED: 5cfb14f — 'Fix: use programmatic electron-rebuild API to avoid bufferutil'
  - scripts/rebuild-sqlite.cjs: calls @electron/rebuild programmatically with
    onlyModules: ['better-sqlite3']. CLI -w/-x flags do NOT reliably skip
    bufferutil (transitive dep of ws). Programmatic onlyModules is the only
    reliable way.
  - win:build: npm run build:electron && node scripts/rebuild-sqlite.cjs && electron-builder --win --x64
  - bufferutil removed from optionalDependencies

COMMITTED: 076ab45 — 'Fix: rename rebuild-sqlite.js to .cjs (package.json has type:module)'
  - package.json has "type": "module" so .js files are treated as ESM
  - require() in the rebuild script threw ReferenceError at runtime
  - Fixed by renaming to .cjs so Node treats it as CommonJS

NOTES FOR YOU (Claude):
  - win:build pipeline is now: esbuild → node scripts/rebuild-sqlite.cjs → electron-builder
  - rebuild-sqlite.cjs MUST stay .cjs — renaming to .js will break the build
  - Do NOT add bufferutil back to any dependencies section — it has no Visual Studio and can't compile
  - If you ever add another native .node module, add it to onlyModules array in scripts/rebuild-sqlite.cjs
  - npmRebuild stays false in package.json build config
